PREFACE
I, the Chairperson of the Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Home
Affairs, having been authorized by the Committee to submit the Report on its behalf, do hereby
present this One Hundred and Thirty First Report on Action Taken by Government on the
recommendations/observations contained in the One Hundred and Twenty Seventh Report on
Demands for Grants (2007-08) of the Ministry of Development of North-Eastern Region.
2. The One Hundred and Twenty Seventh Report of the Department-related Parliamentary
Standing Committee on Home Affairs was presented to Rajya Sabha and laid on the Table of Lok
Sabha on 8 May, 2007.
3. The Ministry of DoNER furnished the Action Taken Replies on the One Hundred and
Twenty Seventh Report of the Committee. The Minister for Development of North Eastern Region
laid on the Table of the Rajya Sabha the status of implementation of the recommendations contained
in the said Report of the Committee, in pursuant to the Chairman, Rajya Sabha’s Direction dated
24th September, 2004, like the previous year, the Committee is again constrained to observe
that both these documents are identical, word-by-word. If the statement of the Minister laid
after nearly four months of the Action Taken Replies sent by the Ministry to the
Secretariat, is a mere reproduction of the ATR, it would defeat the spirit underlying the
Chairman’s Direction.
4. The Committee considered the draft Report and adopted the same at its meeting held on
11th April, 2008.
5. The Recommendations/Observations of the Committee are printed in bold letters.
SUSHMA SWARAJ
N
EW D ELHI; Chairperson,
11th April, 2008 Department-related Parliamentary
Standing Committee on Home Affairs

1
REPORT
The Action Taken Report of the Committee deals with the action taken by the Ministry of
Development of North Eastern Region on the recommendations contained in the One Hundred and
Twenty Seventh Report of the Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Home
Affairs on Demands for Grants (2007-08). The Report was presented to/laid on the Table of Rajya
Sabha and Lok Sabha on the 8 May, 2007.
2. Action Taken Notes have been received from the Ministry of DoNER in respect of the
recommendations contained in the Report. These have been categorized as follows:
Chapter I: The recommendations/observations, which have been accepted by the
Government: Paras: 12.8, 18.3, 20.1, 23.2, 24.2, 25.1;
The Committee is pleased to observe that the Ministry has accepted its recommendation as
mentioned in Chapter–I of the Report.
Chapter II: The recommendations/observations which the Committee does not desire
to pursue in view of the Government’s replies: – Para: 13.3, 13.4, 16.1;
In respect of this recommendation the Committee is convinced with the logic and
explanation advanced by the Ministry and, therefore, does not want to pursue it further.
Chapter III: The recommendations/observations in respect of which the Committee
has not accepted the replies of the Ministry: Paras: 12.7, 14.6, 15.4, 19.6, 21.4, 22.6,
22.7; 27.1
The Committee expresses its concern over the non-implementations of recommendations
contained in Chapter–III and desires that the Ministry should furnish logical explanation in respect
of these recommendations.
Chapter–IV: The recommendations/observations in respect of which final replies of
the Government have not been received: 14.5, 17.3, 24.1, 26.5
In respect of recommendations placed in Chapter–IV , the Ministry has either furnished the
interim replies or couched its response in vague terms. Therefore, the Committee desires that the
Ministry should furnish Action Taken Notes in respect of the recommendations categorized in
Chapter–IV in detail and to the point, as per the intention and spirit of the recommendations of the
Committee.
3. The details of the ATR have been discussed in various Chapters in the succeeding pages.

2
CHAPTER–I
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS WHICH HA VE BEEN
ACCEPTED BY THE GOVERNMENT
RECOMMENDATION
1.1 SURRENDER OF LARGE SUM OF MONEY
1.1.1 The Committee expresses its concern over the surrender of large sums of money by
different Ministries, which ultimately go into NLCPR. Even the Ministries of social sector
are also not able to spend 10 per cent of their budget in the Region. If the national norms
for any particular programme are found to be unsuitable for the North-Eastern Region, the
Ministry concerned should relax the norms according to the conditions of the North-Eastern
States so that the allocation made is spent in the year in which it was allocated.
(Para 12.8)
Action Taken
1.1.2 The Ministries which are surrendering large sums of money have been requested to revise
the norms according to the conditions of North Eastern States so that they are able to utilize the
money allocated in the year of allocation.
RECOMMENDATION
1.2 PROMOTION OF TOURISM AND HOSPITALITY
1.2.1 The Committee feels that the NE region has an excellent untapped tourist potential.
If the potential is fully tapped with sufficient infrastructure, there would be all sided
development of the region including a large number of employment opportunities. The
Committee is happy to note that several private parties are showing interest in the hotel
and tourism sector in North-East. However, there is a long way to go and a lot of investment
is required to develop tourist infrastructure in the NER to make it one of the best tourist
attractions not just of the country but of the world as well. The Committee desires that a
long-term plan and a roadmap may be prepared for creation of tourism infrastructure on
a fast track basis.
(Para 18.3)
Action Taken
1.2.2 The Ministry organized a Special Sectoral Meeting of the North Eastern Council on Tourism
and Hospitality Sector in Gangtok. A number of recommendations were made at the Summit and
the Ministry has initiated follow up action on the recommendations. These include creating
awareness among tourists about the North-East as a safe and attractive destination. The Ministry
has also taken up the matter of relaxing movement of tourists in the North-East. The Ministry has
also taken up the matter with the Ministry of Tourism which has initiated consultation process to
formulate an action plan.
RECOMMENDATION
1.3 ROPEWAY AT TAWANG
1.3.1 The Committee is happy to note that funds had been released for Tawang Ropeway
2

3
in July, 2006 and construction has already started. The Committee recalls that the
foundation for the Ropeway was laid by the President of India way back in 2002. Since there
was no progress in the work, the Committee in its 120th Report of Demands for Grants
(2006-07) expressed its dismay over the extraordinary delay in the matter. Now that the
funds have been released and work has already commenced, the Committee urges upon the
Ministry to ensure that the work is finished as per the target fixed.
(Para 20.1)
Action Taken
1.3.2 The State Government is implementing the projects. Funds have been released and they
have been requested to implement in a time bound manner as per the fixed target.
RECOMMENDATION
1.4 MEDICINAL PLANTS
1.4.1 The Committee is happy to note that emphasis is being given on utilizing the potential of
medicinal plants in the country by the National Medicinal Plants Board. Out of the total allocation
of Rs.80 crore for current financial year, 10 per cent will be spent on NER and similarly about
Rs.100 crore would be available in Eleventh Plan. The Committee recommends that the fund
proposed to be earmarked for the purpose be utilized fully in the region. Appropriate plans may be
drawn for better utilization of the funds. The Committee feels that more positive initiatives need
to be taken to develop the sector in the naturally rich North-East Region.
(Para 23.2)
Action Taken
1.4.2 According to the National Medicinal Plant Board (NMPB), they are making a special effort
to implement the programmes so as to utilize 10% of their budget for the development of medicinal
plant in the North-East. The proposed measures include strengthening of State Medicinal Plant
Boards and preparation of a road map for each State.
RECOMMENDATION
1.5 VISION 2020: Educational Institution
1.5.1 The Committee also reiterates its earlier recommendation for including the
establishment of national leveI sports schools and institutes like National Institute of
Fashion Technology in the region in Vision 2020. Similarly, it also recommends that Road
and Power sectors should form an important part of the document.
(Para 24.2)
Action Taken
1.5.2 The recommendations of the Committee have been conveyed to the NIPFP to keep the same
in view while preparing the Vision NER-2020 document.
RECOMMENDATION
1.6 HEALTH SYSTEM
1.6.1 Considering the different demography, topography and the needs of the region,
national norms of MCI for setting up medical colleges cannot be applied there. The
Committee feels that the norms should not come in the way of providing health
infrastructure in the NE Region. The Committee recommends that the norms may be

4
revised for NER. Steps may also be taken to start medical colleges in every State as
recommended by the Committee earlier.
(Para 25.1)
Action Taken
1.6.2 According to the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, following decisions have been
taken to facilitate setting up of new medical colleges in the Region:
(i) In the past new medical colleges in the country were permitted to utilize the facilities of
other Government/district hospitals for a period of three years from the date of grant of permission
by the Central Government for their establishment, mainly for utilizalion of ciinical material for
teaching purpose. It was stipulated therein that beds of these Government hospitals should be under
the total administrative control of the concerned college and the hospital should be situated within
5 kms. from the medical college. In view of the difficulties being experienced by medical colleges
located in north-eastern, hilly and tribal areas, it has now been decided that the new medical
colleges may be permitted to utilize the facilities of other Government/district hospitals for clinical
material for teaching purpose upto ten years from the date of permission for establishment of
college subject to the condition that beds of these Govt. owned hospitals must be clearly earmarked
for utilization by teaching faculty and further that the academic and clinical control of the patients
must be with the teaching faculty of the medical colleges and the hospital is situated within a
maximum distance of 10 km. from the medical college. The college authorities are, however,
required to ensure that the infrastructure and other facilities in district/Government hospitals being
so utilized are developed as per MCI Regulations.
(ii) The second issue relates to deficiency in faculty of private medical colleges. The Medical
Council of India has allowed a maximum upto 5% deficiency in faculty as condonable because
delay takes place in filling up of the vacancies and some times suitable candidates are not available.
Also the Council has been allowing renewal/recognition of Government Colleges with 10 per cent
faculty deficiency, if the State Government gives assurance/commitment to fill up vacant faculty
positions within a given time. In case of medical colleges established in North Eastern States, hilly
and tribal areas, which are unable to draw maximum number of faculty because of various
conditions, it has been decided that the MCI may hereafter condone 15 per cent deficiency of
faculty at the time of recognition of the institution with the stipulation that the institution would
fill up vacant faculty positions within a given period of three more years and make itself self-
sufficient in every respect.
(iii) The third issue is that indoor bed occupancy in hospitals attached to medical colleges in
North Eastern States, hilly and tribal areas is not upto the stipulated percentage of 80 per cent as
is required as per MCI norms. Considering the hilly and difficult terrain and sparse population in
those areas, MCI may even allow and consider 65 per cent bed occupancy in hospitals attached
to the private medical college in such areas and to encourage private-public partnership while
considering recognition of colleges located in these areas.

5
CHAPTER–II
THE RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS WHICH THE COMMITTEE DOES
NOT DESIRE TO PURSUE IN VIEW OF THE GOVERNMENT’S REPLIES
RECOMMENDATION
2.1 NORTH-EASTERN COUNCIL
2.1.1 The Committee wishes to recall its recommendation made in its One Hundred
Twentieth Report wherein it had expressed its concern that Tenth Plan outlay for NEC had
not been adhered to till 2006-07 which was the terminal year for the Tenth Plan. The
Committee is now informed that the actual allocation to NEC during Tenth Plan has been
Rs.2511.50 crore against Rs.3500 crore. The Committee while reiterating its earlier
recommendation feels that NEC is entitled to an additional allocation of Rs.988.50 crore
during Eleventh Plan as carryover of un allocated outlay from Tenth Plan.
(Para 13.3)
Action Taken
2.1.2 While presenting the demands for allocation for the NEC for Eleventh Five Year Plan, all
the remaining works of the Tenth Plan have been taken into account for adequate allocation in the
Eleventh Plan period.
RECOMMENDATION
2.1 PLAN SCHEME OF NEC
2.2.1 The Committee expresses its concern that though NEC is in a position to absorb the
funds, the Plan schemes of NEC are languishing due to lack of it. The Committee is
surprised to note that there is a committed liability of about Rs.1277 crore for various on
going projects/schemes. With the present allocation, the projects will take a very long time
for completion. In addition, there will be escalation of costs year after year. The better
solution for this could be to transfer funds from NLCPR for the projects of NEC. The funds
that had accrued for a particular sector in NLCPR may be transferred to the same sector
under any NEC projects. The Committee desires that a mechanism may be evolved for such
a transfer of funds to enable the early completion of the Plan projects under NEC. The
Committee also takes note of the fact that certain Plan schemes under NEC would be
transferred to other Ministries. The Committee desires that this may be done at the earliest
so that other Plan schemes may get sufficient funds during the current year.
(Para 13.4)
Action taken
2.2.2 Transfer of NLCPR funds to the projects of NEC is not possible as the committed liabilities
of projects taken up under NLCPR are also quite high and even more than the NEC projects. A
rationalization exercise for Plan schemes under NEC has already been carried out. Some of the
schemes which are adequately taken care of by the schemes of other Central Ministries have been
dropped for the purpose of NEC’s budget allocation. Simultaneously, some of the regional
institutions that were being funded from the Plan Budget of NEC have been transferred to the
concerned line Ministries.
5

6
RECOMMENDATION
2.3 NERAMAC
2.3.1 The Committee was informed that the allocation of Rs.2 crore as loan to NERAMAC
was received at RE 2006-07 stage and this year also the Ministry is hopeful to get the same
at RE stage. The Committee does not appreciate this ad-hoc  approach to such an
organisation like NERAMAC which has one fruit processing unit for the whole of North
East. The Committee also recommends that necessary steps may be taken to strengthen the
organisation. More units of this organisation may be started in various other States in
North-East.
(Para 16.1)
Action Taken
2.3.2 The proposal for loan component for NERAMAC for the 2007-08 has already been sent to
the Integrated Finance Division for re-appropriation from some other provision in the budget of this
Ministry. NERAMAC already has two working units. The third unit for ginger processing has also
started to function in Meghalaya. Efforts are on to have a fourth unit in Assam for cashew
processing. However, more efforts are being made from the organization towards procurement of
farmers produce so as to benefit them directly.

7
CHAPTER–III
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS IN RESPECT OF WHICH EITHER THE
REPLIES OF GOVERNMENT HAVE NOT BEEN ACCEPTED BY COMMITTEE
OR COMMITTEE DESIRES TO MAKE FURTHER RECOMMENDATION
RECOMMENDATION
3.1 NON-LAPSABLE CENTRAL POOL OF RESOURCES (NLCPR)
3.1.1 The Committee is happy to note that this year, no allocation has been made out of
NLCPR funds, for Bodo Territorial Council and Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan Schemes, as
recommended by the Committee last year. The Committee is also happy to note that the
Ministry has reviewed the Exempted List of Ministries/Departments in respect of allocation
of 10 per cent of the budget allocation to North-Eastern States. However, the Committee
expresses its concern that even after the review, only the Department of Biotechnology has
been taken out of the List of Exempted Ministries. The Committee, therefore, reiterates its
recommendation made in the 120th Report on Demands for Grants for 2006-07 that the
other Ministries also may be taken out from the List of Exempted Ministries/Departments.
(Para 12.7)
Action Taken
3.1.2 After a thorough review with the Ministries concerned, the exemption of Department of
Bio-Technology has been withdrawn and some of the Ministries which have some scope available
for expenditure in the North Eastern Region were asked to provide maximum possible percentage
of GBS for the North Eastern Region.
Further Recommendation
3.1.3 The Committee reiterates its recommends that Government may consider the matter
again and take out some more Ministries from the list of exempted Ministries.
RECOMMENDATION
3.2 UNDUE DELAY IN PILOT AND AIRHOSTESS TRAINING
3.2.1 The Committee expresses its concern over the undue and uncalled for delay in pilot
and airhostess training. It is surprising to note that in the entire year the process of
identifying the institute for training could not be completed. The Committee takes strong
exception to such avoidable delays which also result in cost overrun. Tbe Committee
recommends that the process of identifying the institute may be completed within next
three months and the training may be conducted at the earliest.
(Para 14.6)
Action Taken
3.2.2 In order to expedite the process of selection of suitable institutes for training of pilots and
air hostesses, the Ministry constituted a Committee. The bidding process has been completed and
the proposals have been sent for financial concurrence.
7

8
Further Recommendation
3.2.3 The Committee expresses its disquiet over the continuing delay in identifying the
institute for pilot and airhostess training. The Committee recommends that the institutes
may be selected immediately so that training may start without further delay.
RECOMMENDATION
3.3 EXTERNALLY AIDED PROJECTS
3.3.1 The Committee while appreciating the efforts of the Ministry in coming out with
several projects under the Externally Aided Projects scheme, reiterates its earlier
recommendation that the faster such schemes are processed the better it would be. The
Planning Commission may give ‘in principle’ approval for the North Eastern State Roads
Project early so that the remaining processes may be completed during the current financial
year and the project started. The Committee also strongly recommends that at least the
first phase of North Eastern Urban Development Project may be put in place during the
current financial year. The Committee cautions the Ministry about the user charges to be
recovered in six years. This aspect should be carefully considered before taking a final view.
The Committee is also of the view that the 10 per cent loan component, which has been
assigned to the State Governments to be raised on their own, should be re-examined in light
of the difficulties being faced by the North East States.
(Para 15.4 )
Action Taken
3.3.2 (a) For the North Eastern State Roads Project, ‘in-principle’ approval of the Planning
Commission has been received. The Planning Commission has stated that Ministry of DONER will
avail loan from ADB amounting to 70 per cent of the project cost while balance 30 per cent of
the project cost will be borne by the Government of India and the funds will be released to the
State Governments as 100 per cent grant treating it as Centrally Sponsored Scheme. The project
proposal is under process for EFC’s approval and then approval of the Cabinet/CCEA.
3.3.3 (b) The Ministry of DONER had taken up the matter with the Ministry of Urban
Development for transfer of North Eastern Urban Development Project (NEUDP) so as to avoid
duplication in the efforts of the two Ministries in the implementation of the instant ADB project
and the Jawaharlal Nehru National Urban Renewal Mission (JNNURM) as there are lot of
commonalities between the two Ministry of Urban Development has since conveyed acceptance of
transfer of this project to their Ministry. The concerns of the Hon’ble Committee are being
conveyed to the MoUD.
Further Recommendation
3.3.4 The Committee apprehends that both the projects, viz. North Eastern Urban
Development Project (NEUDP) and Jawaharlal Nehru National Urban Renewal Mission
(JNNURM) may be delayed in the process of approval and transfer. The Committee desires
that these projects should start without any further delay.
RECOMMENDATION
3.4 CIVIL A VIATION
3.4.1 The Committee while noting the reply of the Ministry is of the opinion that civil
aviation should be declared a priority sector for NER. It also feels that the Government
should be more proactive in implementing its announcement for the region and sectors like

9
Civii Aviation should get priority and special impetus. The Committee’s considered view is
that a boost to civil aviation in the region and improving air connectivity within the region
as well as from the rest of tbe country is of paramount importance if the region has to be
brought to the mainstream. The Committee recommends that all the airports in the NER
may be upgraded at the earliest. The Committee is dismayed over the fact that Planning
Commission has yet not given the ‘in principle’ approval for ‘Teju’ airport, despite the
recommendation made by it in its 120th Report on Demands for Grants (2006-07) of
Ministry of DoNER. The Committee is also of the view that the offer of the Ministry of
Defence for providing trained pilots on permanent absorption basis should be gladly accepted
by the Ministry of Civil Aviation, if it is really serious about development of civil aviation
in the region and that Ministry should take early decisions on such important proposals.
They should also expedite the matter relating to technical assistance for the Pilot Training
Institute at Lilabari.
(Para 19.6)
Action Taken
3.4.2 Government has been making special efforts in Civil Aviation sector. A full Council Summit
of NEC was held to review schemes and programmes under this sector in Aizawl in the month
of May, 2007.
3.4.3 The Annual Plan 2007-08 of NEC has identified Connectivity, including air connectivity as
one of the priority sectors for North East. Intra region air connectivity as well as connectivity with
the rest of the country needs to be substantially augmented. In view of the same, efforts are
continuously being made to improve infrastructure and other facilities for better air connectivity in
the North Eastern Region. There are 12 operational airports in NER, at present. The NEC has
entered into a MoU with the AAI for funding upgradation of 10 airports in the ratio of 60:40. Work
on 7 airports has since been completed and is continuing at 3 airports. An amount of
Rs.50.00 crore has been earmarked for ongoing upgradation works of airports in NER in the
Annual Plan, during 2007-08. In addition to the upgradation of existing airports, upgradation of
non-operational airports is also proposed to be undertaken during Eleventh Plan. NEC has kept
provision in its Annual Plan for supporting DPR preparation and the Airports Authority of India has
been requested to prepare the DPRs for the upgradation of 5 non-operational airports at Kalashar
and Kamlapur in Tripura, Pasighat and Tezu in Arunachal Pradesh and Tura in Meghalaya.
3.4.5 The Planning Commission has granted “in principle” approval to the upgradation of airport
at Pasight on 8th November, 2006 and to the upgradation of airport at Tezu on 23.4.2007.
However, Planning Commission has directed that the project be implemented by the Airports
Authority of India (AAI) and be funded through a mix of internal accruals of AAI and Gross
Budgetary Support in the ratio of 1:1. This has been conveyed to the Ministry of Civil Aviation,
the Airports Authority of India (AAI) and the NEC.
3.4.6 The Ministry of Defence have informed that IAF have a vast pool of trained pilots and
technical staff who could be spared for gainful utilization by Indian Airlines/Alliance Air only on
permanent absorption basis. This has been conveyed to the Ministry of Civil Aviation. Response is
awaited.
Further Recommendation
3.4.7 The Committee reiterates its observation that inter and intra air connectivity of NER
would prove a sine qua non  for the all round development of North Eastern Region, be it
a tourist destiny or economic development or inducement investment. The Committee,
therefore, strongly, recommends that the Ministry of DoNER should not confine itself

10
merely to forwarding the development projects from one Ministry to the other but, being
the territorial Ministry endowed with role and responsibility of developing the North-Eastern
Region, should play pro-active and result-oriented role in pursuing continuously so far as
the inception and implementation of the proposal/undertaken projects are concerned viz.
improvement of inter and intra region air services; setting up of Greenfield airports at
Kohima, Itanagar, Gangtok and for upgradation of airports of Pasight and Tezu in Arunachal
Pradesh, Baljek in West Garo Hills, Meghalaya and Kamalpur and Kailashar in Tripura.
These projects should be completed within the stipulated time frame and should not incur
time and cost overruns. The Committee further recommends that the Ministry of DoNER
should take adequate follow up action with the Ministry of Civil Aviation for harnessing the
vast pool of trained pilots and technical staff of IAF by inducting them on permanent
absorption basis.
RECOMMENDATION
3.5 PROMOTION OF INDUSTRIES
3.5.1 The Committee notes the contents of the North-East Industrial and Investment
Promotion Policy (NEIIPP), 2007 vis-a-vis NE Industrial Policy, 1997 and also the negative
list whereunder industries like Tobacco, Pan Masala, Plastic Carry bags of less than 20
microns and some specified goods produced by petroleum oil and gas refineries are not
eligible for benefits under NEIIPP, 2007. The Committee feels t hat the incentives and
subsidies mentioned in the new policy if implemented in the right earnest would go a long
way in giving a fillip to the tourism, hospitality and power sectors. The Committee is also
of the considered view that considering the region’s diversity, the Government should
ensure that the small scale and agro based industries get support in the new Industrial
Policy.
(Para 21.4)
Action Taken
3.5.2 Department of Industrial Policy and Promotion (Government of India) as well as North
Eastern Development Finance Corporation (NEDFC) have been advised to ensure that the small
scale and agro-based industries get support under the new industrial policy.
Further Recommendation
3.5.3 The Committee feels that the Ministry of DoNER should not ony pro-actively liase
and take follow-up initiatives/action with the Department of IPP, (Government of India) and
NEDFC (North Eastern Development Finance Corporation) but should also interact with the
Ministry of Small, Micro and Medium Enterprises for promoting micro, small and medium
enterprises in the NE region.
RECOMMENDATION
3.6 AGRICULTURE SECTOR
3.6.1 The Committee agrees that agriculture sector plays a predominant role in the North-
Eastern Region. There is a huge potential for increasing the revenue and the allied
industries in the North-Eastern Region by which employment opportunities can be increased
and there can be more income-generating activities. However, the investment being made
by NEC under agriculture and allied sector is only 1.74 per cent of the total Plan allocation
which is very meagre and it will not have any significant impact. The Committee, therefore,
recommends that allocation may be increased for agricultural activities under the Plan

11
allocation of NEC. Similarly, the Ministry of Agriculture may also increase the agricultural
and allied activities in the North-Eastern Region. The Committee feels happy to learn that
Bamboo Mission was initiated during 2006-07 with a budget of Rs.568.23 crore. If the
Mission is implemented in the right earnest, it is going to have a great impact on the
economy of the States.
(Para 22.6)
Action Taken
3.6.2 Agriculture is the S tate subject and the Ministry of Agriculture has large number of schemes
including those for horticulture sector. NEC though concentrates on infrastructure development in
the Region, takes care of agriculture and allied activities for agriculture and allied sector, which
have increased to 2.2 per cent. It is also in view of the fact that Ministry of Agriculture are not
able to spend their entire allocation in the NER.
3.6.3 The budget allocation of the NEC for 2007-08 has not been increased and it has been
retained at Rs. 600 crore. Moreover, a large number of spill over works are required to be
completed. However, in the Annual Plan 2007-08 of NEC, an outlay of Rs. 10.42 crores has been
provided for Agriculture and Allied sector. The Ministry of Agriculture has also been requested to
take action as suggested by the Committee.
3.6.4 The National Bamboo Mission (NBM) has been approved at a cost of Rs. 568.23 crore. The
scheme is being implemented by Ministry of Agriculture.
Further Recommendation
3.6.5 The Committee is constrained to note that the Ministry of Agriculture is not able to
spend their entire allocation in the NER. The Ministry of Agriculture must ensure that the
allocated budget is spent.
RECOMMENDATION
3.7 PROBLEMS AND PROSPECTS OF AGRICULTURAL SECTOR
3.7.1 The Committee takes a serious note of the fact that the small tea growers in Assam,
who are about 50,000 in number, do not have pattas due to which they are not able to carry
out any improvements on the land nor are they able to get loans. The Committee makes
a strong recommendation that immediate steps may be taken to ensure that the small tea
growers are issued pattas at the earliest. The Committee also agrees that the North-Eastern
States have a great potential for rubber production. The Committee expresses its concern
that production of rubber in the North-Eastern States has not been taken up very seriously
so far. The Report of the Committee set up by NEC under one of the full-time Members,
if submitted, may be examined thoroughly and immediate steps may be taken to introduce
rubber plantation in the North-Eastern States wherever it has potential. If necessary,
separate technology mission may be initiated for this purpose exclusively for North-Eastern
States with separate budgetary provision. The Committee takes note of the fact that North-
Eastern States have a great potential for ginger production. However, there is no proper
system for marketing and for processing of the ginger produced to enable the farmers to
sell their produce at a profitable rate. The Committee is happy to learn that the initiative
already taken by the Government has been very successful but the Government should not
be complacent with this. This is only an initial effort and a lot more has to be done for
marketing of the produces such as ginger of the North-Eastern States. The Committee,
therefore, recommends that processing facilities may be established for all the agricultural
produce along with marketing facilities.
(Para 22.7)

12
Action Taken
3.7.2 The State Governments of North Eastern Region have been requested for taking action on
the point of issuance of pattas to the small growers. A Task Force has been constituted under the
Chairmanship of Shri P.P. Shrivastav, Member, NEC to examine the existing central programmes,
identify gap and recommend specific measures for promoting rubber plantation in the selected areas
of the region. Three meetings of the Task Force have been held so far with the Nodal Officers
of Assam, Arunachal Pradesh, Manipur; Meghalaya, Mizoram and Nagaland Governments to discuss
the strategies for implementation of rubber plantation in the region. The consultation meetings were
held with the State Governments. Detailed Project Reports are awaited from them. For procurement
and marketing of ginger and other agricultural/horticultural produce, efforts have been enhanced.
Ginger processing has been started in the plant established by the Ministry.
Further Recommendations
3.7.3 The Committee desires that pattas may be issued to the small tea growers at the
earliest. The Committee also desires that the projects reports may be obtained from State
Governments on Rubber Plantations and the Task Force may finalize its recommendations
at the earliest.
RECOMMENDATION
3.8 SPECIAL INITIATIVES
3.8.1 The Committee is happy to note that in the meeting chaired by the Prime Minister
on 16.10.2006, decisions had been taken inter-alia  that the line Ministries would consult
Ministry of DoNER before finalizing any scheme to be implemented in North East. The
Committee recommends that this decision should be formalized by incorporating the same
in the Allocation of Business Rules, 1961 and by effectively communicating the same to all
Ministries/Departments so that there is no confusion in any quarter in this regard.
(Para 27.1)
Action Taken
3.8.2 In this connection Cabinet Secretary had already written to all the Secretaries to
Government of India to consult Ministry of DoNER before finalizing any scheme to be implemented
in the North East. The Ministry has requested the Cabinet Secretariat to make appropriate provision
in the Government of India (Allocation of Business) Rules, 1961.
Further Recommendation
3.8.3 The Committee desires that the Cabinet Secretariat may make the provision in the
Government of India (Allocation of Business) Rules, 1961 as the earliest, that the line
Ministries would consult the Ministry of DoNER before finalizing any scheme to be
implemented in North East.

13
CHAPTER–IV
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS IN RESPECT OF WHICH
FINAL REPLIES OF GOVERNMENT HA VE NOT BEEN RECEIVED
RECOMMENDATION
4.1 ADVOCACY, PUBLICITY, CAPACITY BUILDING  AND TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE
4.1.1 The Committee do recognise the importance of showcasing North East through Plan
Schemes such as Advocacy and Publicity and appreciates the efforts of the Ministry under
where it had taken such programmes in capital cities and other cities of various States
during last year. The Committee however wants to impress upon the Ministry to adopt some
innovative methods.
(Para 14.5)
Action Taken
4.1.2 The Ministry has initiated new approaches for showcasing the potential and the strength of
the North-East. Recently, a North-East Business Summit was organized. Further as an step to
attract investment we facilitated a visit of a high level business delegation from Thailand. The
Ministry has also proposed to show case the NER abroad through various events in collaboration
with organizations like CII and ICC. A Committee has been constituted to prepare a media plan for
projecting the North-East as a safe and attractive destination through electronic and print media.
RECOMMENDATION
4.2 GOVERNMENT OF INDIA ( ALLOCATION OF BUSINESS) RULES, 1961
4.2.1 The Committee is concerned that even though the two programmes i.e., Hill Area
Development Programme (HADP) and Border Area Development Programme (BADP) are
shown in tbe Government of India (Allocation of Business) Rules, 1961 to be with the
Ministry of DoNER but the programmes are yet to be transferred to it. The Committee feels
that it is not right on the part of the Government to show the programmes against a
Ministry without transferring them to it. The Committee recommends that the issue may
be resolved expeditiously.
(Para 17.3)
Action Taken
4.2.2 The Ministry has already requested the Cabinet Secretariat for resolving this Issue.
RECOMMENDATION
4.3 VISION NER 2020
4.3.1 The Vision document is undoubtedly the most ambitious project of NEC since its
inception. To achieve the developmental goals of a region, which has lagged far behind from
the mainstream, such measures are a necessity. The final version of the document was
scheduled to be in place by June, 2006. The Committee is of the view that of the fifteen
years period, two more years would be lost in finalizing the document. Hence, it feels that
efforts be taken to complete such an ambitious document on time, without further delay.
(Para 24.1)
13

14
Action Taken
4.3.2 NEC has entrusted the National Institute of Public Finance and Policy (NIPFP), New Delhi
to Prepare Vision NER-2020. The Institute has agreed to submit the final document within a period
of 9 months i.e. by November 2007
RECOMMENDATION
4.4 TRADE PROMOTION
4.4.1 Trade promotion is an important aspect for the development of any region and the
North-Eastern Region is no exception to it. The existing infrastructure is very inadequate
to give sufficient avenues to the North-Eastern Region for trade promotion. The Committee
recommends that the Ministry may make an overall assessment of the requirement of trade
promotion activities for the North-Eastern Region and necessary steps may be taken in this
regard. The trade centre proposed to be set up at Guwahati is a good proposal for promoting
trade and industry not only in Assam but in the entire North-Eastern Region. The
Committee, therefore, recommends that the Centre may be commissioned as early as
possible so that it may commence functioning soon. The project for the North-Eastern
States’ Trade and Investment Creative Initiative undcrtaken with the technical assistance
of Asian Development Bank (ADB) is an important project for the overall growth of trade
and industry in the North-Eastern States. The Draft Report submitted by the ADB
Consultants may be examined at the earliest and a final decision may be taken soon to
make the project functional. The Committee also learned that the North-Eastern States are
asking for more land custom stations and development of infrastructure in the existing
stations. The Committee recommends that the Ministry may examine these issues and take
up with the concerned Ministries and take an early decision. Development of infrastructure
at the custom stations is very essential because without proper infrastructure, the custom
stations will not be successful. The Ministry of DoNER may consider this aspect and take
up the infrastructure development for custom stations on a priority basis with separate
allocation, if required.
(Para 26.5)
Action Taken
4.4.2 As per Min istry of Commerce, the infrastructure for the International Trade Promotion
Centre at Guwahati is in place. The centre is likely to be commissioned shortly. Another Centre
in the name of “North Eastern Agri-Expo Centre” at Dimapur, Nagaland sanctioned, under NLCPR
scheme of Ministry of DONER, for establishment.
4.4.3 Ministry of DONER through Technical Assistance (TA) of Asian Development Bank (ADB)
seeks to develop a project for the North Eastern States Trade and Investment Creative Initiative
(NES-TICI) so as to build on the locational advantage of the NER States with international borders
with five countries. Draft study report prepared through ADB assistance was discussed with the
NE States and other stakeholders in a Regional Workshop held at Guwahati. It was circulated to
all the stakeholders and the consultations are on to finalise the report taking into consideration
the new North East Industrial and Investment Promotion Policy (NEIIPP) 2007 launched from
1st April, 2007.

PREFACE
I, the Chairperson of the Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Home
Affairs having been authorised by the Committee to submit the report on its behalf, do hereby
present this One Hundred and Thirty second Report on Demands for Grants (2008-09) relating to
the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA).
2. While examining Demands for Grants every year, it has been the practice in this Committee
to take up one subject/issue for special focus. It had earlier taken up “Disaster Management”,
“Delhi Police and its functioning” and “Union Territories without Legislature” focused study during
2005-06, 2006-07 and 2007-08, respectively. In the current year, the Committee had decided to
highlight “Naxalism” in its report. To facilitate in-depth examination of the subject by the
Committee, the officials of the Home Ministry made an exclusive presentation in the matter before
it. However, keeping in view the wide ranging implications of the subject, the Committee decided
to make a detailed study of the subject and present a separate report after taking into account the
views of the affected State Governments.
3. The Committee held in all three sittings to complete the examination of Demands for Grants
of the Ministry of Home Affairs. The Committee heard the Home Secretary on Demands for Grants
(2008-09) of Ministry of Home Affairs and Naxalism in its meetings held on 28th March and 5th
April, 2008, respectively.
4. The Committee while making its observations/recommendations has mainly relied upon the
following:—
(i) Presentations made by the Home Secretary and other concerned officers;
(ii) Detailed Demands for Grants of the Ministry for the year 2008-09;
(iii) Annual Report of the Ministry of Home Affairs for the year 2007-08;
(iv) Outcome Budget of the Ministry for the year 2008-09;
(v) Detailed Explanatory Note on the Demands for Grants of the Ministry of Home Affairs
for the year 2008-09;
(vi) Physical and financial targets fixed and achieved during the Tenth Plan period and the
breakdown of the same for the year 2008-09 of the Eleventh Plan;
(vii) Projection of outlays for the schemes to be undertaken by the Ministry during the
Eleventh Five Year Plan;
(viii) Details of under-utilization of the allocations made under different heads during the last
three years;
(ix) Written replies furnished by the Ministry to the Questionnaires sent to them by the
Secretariat; and
(x) Written clarifications furnished by the Ministry, on the points/issues raised by the
Members during the deliberations of the Committee.
5. The Committee considered and adopted this report in its sitting held on 11th April, 2008.

6. For facility of reference and convenience, observations and recommendations of the
Committee have been printed in bold letters in the body of the Report.

CHAPTER-I
OVERVIEW
Maintenance of internal security, management of para-military forces, border management,
Centre-State relations, administration of Union Territories, disaster management are the major
responsibilities of the Ministry of Home Affairs. In addition, the Ministry also has the following
broad responsibilities:
(i) Issue of Notification in respect of Appointment of President/Vice-President, Prime
Minister and Members of the Union Council of Ministers;
(ii) Appointment of Governors and Lt. Governors;
(iii) Regulation of Pay and Allowances of the Ministers;
(iv) Carrying out Census in India once every ten years;
(v) Implementation of the Provisions of the Official Language Act, 1963;
(vi) Maintenance of Communal Harmony and Promotion of National Integration;
(vii) Co-ordination of Policy relating to Human Rights;
(viii) Providing Relief and Rehabilitation to Refugees/Displaced Persons;
(ix) Regulation of Entry of Foreigners into India;
(x) Grant of Pension and Other Benefits to Freedom Fighters; and
(xi) Prevention and Combat of Drug Abuse and Drug Trafficking.
2. To discharge the above responsibilities, the Ministry has been divided into following six
constituent Departments:
(i) Department of Internal Security;
(ii) Department of States;
(iii) Department of Home;
(iv) Department of Jammu and Kashmir (J and K) Affairs;
(v) Department of Border Management; and
(vi) Department of Official Language.
2.1 The Department of Internal Security deals with Indian Police Service, Central Police
Forces, internal security and law and order, insurgency, terrorism, naxalism, activities of inimical
foreign agencies, rehabilitation, grant of visa and other immigration matters, security clearances, etc.
2.2 Department of States deals with Centre-State relations, Inter-State relations, administration
of Union Territories, freedom fighters’ pension, human rights, prison reforms, police reforms, etc.
2.3 Department of Home deals with notification of assumption of office by the President and
Vice-President, notification of appointment/resignation of the Prime Minister, Ministers, Governors,
nomination to Rajya Sabha/Lok Sabha, census of population, registration of births and deaths, etc.

2
2.4 Department of Jammu and Kashmir Affairs deals with the constitutional provisions in
respect of the State of Jammu and Kashmir and all other matters relating to the State, excluding
those with which the Ministry of External Affairs is concerned.
2.5 Department of Border Management deals with management of international borders
including coastal borders, strengthening of border guarding and creation of related infrastructure,
border areas development, etc.
2.6 Department of Official Language is concerned with the implementation of the provisions
of the Constitution relating to official languages and the provisions of the Official Language
Act, 1963.
3. The Ministry is under the overall charge of the Minister of Home Affairs assisted by three
Ministers of State. All Departments of the Ministry except the Department of Official Language are
interlinked and are headed by the Home Secretary who is assisted by Secretary (Border
Management), two Special Secretaries, three Additional Secretaries and nineteen Joint Secretaries.
The Department of Official Language has a separate Secretary and functions independently. The
Ministry is further divided into eighteen divisions for administrative purposes and is concerned with
the tasks mentioned below for each division:-
(i) Centre State Division
The Division deals with Central-State relations, including working of the Constitutional
provisions governing such relations; appointment of Governors; creation of new
States; nominations to Rajya Sabha/Lok Sabha; Inter-State boundary disputes; over-
seeing the crime situation in States; imposition of President’s Rule; etc.
(ii) Internal Security Division
The Division deals with matters relating to internal security, including anti-national and
subversive activities of various groups/extremist organizations; policy and operational
issues on terrorism; Narcotics Control Bureau; National Security Act; etc.
(iii) Police Division
The Division functions as the cadre controlling authority of IPS officers and also
deals with all matters relating to Central Police Forces, including their deployment.
(iv) Union Territories Division
The Division deals with all legislative and constitutional matters relating to Union
Territories including Delhi and Puducherry. It also functions as the cadre controlling
authority of Arunachal Pradesh-Goa-Mizoram and Union Territories (AGMUT) Cadre
of IAS/IPS as also Delhi-Andaman Nicobar Islands Civil Service (DANICS)/Delhi-
Andaman Nicobar Islands Police Service (DANIPS). It is also responsible for
overseeing the crime and law and order situation in UTs.
(v) North-Eastern Division
The Division deals with the law and order situation in North-Eastern States, including
matters relating to insurgency and talks with various extremist groups operating in
that region.
(vi) Jammu and Kashmir Division
The Division deals with the Constitutional matters including Article 370 and general
policy matters in respect of J and K and terrorism/militancy in that State; it is also
responsible for implementation of the PM’s Package for J and K.
(vii) Foreigners Division
The Division deals with all matters relating to visa, Protected Area Permit/Restricted

3
Area Permit regime, immigration, citizenship, overseas citizenship of India, acceptance
of foreign contribution and hospitality.
(viii) Freedom Fighters and Rehabilitation Division
The Division frames and implements the Freedom Fighters Pension Scheme and the
schemes for rehabilitation of migrants from former West Pakistan/East Pakistan and
provision of relief to Srilankan and Tibetan refugees.
(ix) Human Rights Division
The Division deals with matters relating to the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993
and also matters relating to national integration, communal harmony and Ayodhya
affairs.
(x) Disaster Management Division
This division is bifurcated into two parts: Disaster Management-I Division is
responsible for response, relief and preparedness for natural calamities and man-made
disasters (except drought and epidemics), whereas Disaster Management-II Division
is responsible for legislation, policy, capacity building, prevention, mitigation and long
term rehabilitation.
(xi) Border Management Division
This Division deals with all matters relating to management of international borders,
including coastal borders, creation of infrastructure like integrated check posts, road/
fencing and floodlighting of borders and the Border Area Development Programme.
(xii) Police Modernization Division
The Division handles all items of work relating to modernisation of State Police
Forces, provisioning/procurement of various items for modernisation of Central
Police Forces, police reforms and security of VIPs/vitals installation.
(xiii) Policy Planning Division
It deals with meetings of the SAARC Interior/Home Ministers, matters relating to
policy formulation in respect of internal security issues, international cooperation on
counter-terrorism, international covenants, bilateral assistance treaties and related
items of work.
(xiv) Finance Division
The Division is responsible for formulating, operating and controlling the budget of
the Ministry under the Integrated Finance Scheme.
(xv) Judicial Division
The Division deals with all matters relating to the legislative aspects of the Indian
Penal Code, 1860, Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 and the Commissions of Inquiry
Act, 1952. It also handles matters relating to the State legislations to the extent such
legislation require the assent of the President under the Constitution; political pension
to erstwhile rulers before independence and mercy petitions under Article 72 of the
Constitution.
(xvi) Administration Division
The Division is responsible for handling all administrative and vigilance matters of the
Ministry of Home Affairs, monitoring of compliance of furnishing information under
the Right to Information Act, 2005 and it also deals with matters relating to Table of
Precedence, Bharat Ratna and Padma Awards, Gallantry Awards, Jeevan Raksha
Padak, National Flag, National Anthem, State Emblem of India and Secretariat Security
Organisation.

4
(xvii) Coordination Division
The division deals with intra-Ministry coordination work, Parliamentary matters,
public grievances, publication of Annual Report of the Ministry, Record Retention
Schedule, custody of classified and non-classified records of the Ministry, Internal
Work Study, furnishing of various reports relating to employment of SCs/STs and
persons with Disabilities to Department of Personnel and Training, etc.
(xviii) Naxal Management Division
This Division was created w.e.f. October, 29, 2006 in the Ministry to effectively
tackle the naxalite menace from both security and development angles. It monitors the
naxal situation and counter-measures being taken by the affected States with the
objective of improving ground-level policing and development response as per the
location specific action plans formulated/to be formulated by the affected States and
review with the concerned Ministries/Departments to ensure optimum utilization of
funds released and proper implementation of various developmental schemes in the
naxal affected areas.

CHAPTER–III
SCHEMES, POLICIES AND PROGRAMMES OF THE MINISTRY
Multipurpose National Identity Cards Scheme
9.0 The Committee notes that the Government has taken up implementation of a pilot project
for preparing a National Register of Indian Citizens and issue of Multipurpose National Identity
Cards (MNIC) to all citizens of the country. The main purpose of this is to provide a credible
individual identification system and simultaneous use of this card for several multifarious socio-
economic benefits and transactions within and outside the country.
9.1 An amount of Rs.44.36 crore has been sanctioned for MNIC pilot project. Of this,
Rs.38.36 crore is for the implementation of the project and another Rs.6.00 crore for testing and
running the project for one year from the date of completion. As stated by the Ministry of Home
Affairs, twenty one lakh ninety four thousand persons have been verified for their status as citizens
out of the total targeted population of twenty eight lakh sixty two thousand persons. Three lakh
seventy thousand persons are in the process of being verified and two lakh ninety eight thousand
could not be verified due to various reasons. Of the twenty one lakh ninety four thousand verified
persons, thirteen lakh forty seven are of the age of 18 years and above and nearly twelve lakh
persons have been issued identity cards as on date and another fifty thousand persons are expected
to be issued the card additionally. The Committee has also been given to understand that the pilot
project would be completed by 31.03.2008.
9.2 It was further stated by the Ministry that the pilot project would be continued for one year
to record the changes in the citizen database as well as issue of identity cards to those who had
been either left out in the past or those who attained the age of 18 years in the next one year or
those who come to reside in the pilot areas thereafter. Accordingly to the Ministry, nearly two to
three lakh cards are expected to be additionally personalized during 2008-09.
9.3 On being asked about the next course of action of the Ministry, after this pilot project, the
Home Secretary stated as under:—
“A scheme is going on which is called the Unique Identity Number Scheme, which is
being implemented by the Department of Information and Technology under the overall
supervision of the Planning Commission. The main aim is for better administration in
programmes like Public Distribution System, issue of Below Poverty Line (BPL) cards.
Under this scheme, a primary database is created by the collation of Election
Commission, computerized database based on the voter list and whatever database is
available relating to the BPL Scheme, and they have already been able to, according
to our last discussion, get the records of sixty eight crore people. A Group of Ministers
(GoM) has been constituted to see how the MNIC scheme and UID scheme can be
converged.”
9.4 The Committee expresses its strong displeasure on the adhocism adopted by the
Government. The MNIC scheme was launched on pilot basis prior to the announcement of
the UID scheme. The Planning Commission should have obtained status as well as feedback
on the MNIC Scheme and then taken a decision on any other scheme, let alone UID
21

22
scheme. Running of two parallel schemes appear to be overlapping in objectives and may
be perceived to be wastage of time and resource. Implementation of the pilot project for
MNIC has taken unduly long time and yet it is not known how long it would take to
complete the Scheme in the entire country and on top of that another scheme has been
launched. The Committee recommends that the Group of Ministers may critically review the
MNIC and UID Schemes and examine the feasibility of merging the two into a single
integrated programme, so as to avoid overlapping of objectives and likely wastage of
resource and manpower. Whatever may be the recommendation of the Committee,
Government must ensure that such a programme should be made feasible for
implementation within a reasonable and strictive time-frame.
Modernization of Police Forces
10.0 The law and order situation and crime scenario have made it imperative to modernise the
State Police Forces quickly. The State Police, being directly concerned with the law and order,
there is a need to improve their functioning and to equip them with the latest technology so that
they are able to successfully meet emerging challenges. To supplement the efforts of the State
Government/UT administration in modernizing their police forces, the Ministry of Home Affairs has
been implementing a Non-Plan Scheme of Modernization of Police Force (MPF). It is also
necessary for capacity building of the State Police Forces (SPF), especially for meeting the
emerging challenges to internal security in the form of terrorism, naxalism, etc. The main objective
of the scheme is to reduce the dependence of the State Governments on the Army and Central
Police Forces to control internal security and law and order situation by way of equipping the State
Police Forces adequately. The scheme also aims at a balanced development of the State Police
Forces.
10.1 The Committee in its 119th Report had recommended for extension of this important
scheme to UTs and further recommended for necessary allocation at RE stage in 2006-07. As a
result, provision was made for the Modernization of Police Forces in UTs at RE stage for the year.
For the year 2008-09, an amount of Rs.1340.63 crore has been allocated under this head. Out of
this Rs.1163.83 crore is for assistance to States for modernization of their police. Whereas
Rs.41.20 crore and Rs.13.20 crore are for UTs without legislature and UTs with legislature,
respectively. Rs.122.40 crore has been provided for assistance to Delhi Police for modernization.
10.2 The Ministry in its reply to a question has stated that the main components included under
the Scheme are construction of secure police stations, outposts, police lines, mobility, modern
weaponry, security, Surveillance, communication, forensic equipment, upgradation of training
infrastructure, police housing, computerization etc. The States have formulated and submitted their
annual action plans broadly covering these aspects and also on the assessment of their needs taking
into consideration the prevailing ground situation.
10.3 Explaining about the importance of the scheme, the Ministry in the Annual Report stated as
under:
“The scheme has made perceptible impact on all the States and has provided much-
needed assistance and impetus to police modernization. For instance, proper buildings
for police stations/outposts with required facilities have provided a safe, secure and
comfortable environment, construction of houses for police personnel and provision of
modern weapons have boosted their morale, particularly in extremist-affected areas.
The increased availability of vehicles at cutting edge level has improved mobility and
reduced response time.”

23
10.4 On being asked about whether the Government has any monitoring mechanism to ensure
the optimum utilization of funds, the Ministry has stated that the State Governments are periodically
persuaded to ensure optimum utilization of funds and furnishing utilization certificates in regard to
the central funds released during previous years. It was further stated that visits by central teams
are also undertaken for monitoring the implementation of the Scheme in the States and the matter
regarding optimum utilization of funds under the MPF is reviewed from time to time, in
consultation with concerned States.
10.5 The Committee observes that the role of the Ministry is not confined to merely
allocating funds to the States but it has the responsibility to ensure that each and every
rupee is spent in the furtherance of the objective of the scheme. The Committee reiterates
its recommendations made in the earlier reports that it should be insisted upon all the
States to send utilization certificates at the earliest in order to ensure that States spend the
funds meant for modernization of their police forces in an efficient manner.
10.6 The Committee observed that the major component of the Scheme is construction of
residential and non-residential buildings for police forces. It is the view of the Committee
that though allocation of funds for construction of police housing and other buildings are
equally important and definitely enhance the morale of the police forces, yet it should not
be done at the cost of modernization of police forces. The Committee is constrained to note
that after nearly eight years of commencement of this Scheme, there are hardly any
perceptible changes in the functioning of police stations. The Committee feels that housing
for police is the basic necessity and it should not be clubbed with modernization. If
necessary, Government may separate the component of housing from modernization and
provide separate grant for the former. The Committee recommends that ‘modernization’
should appropriately include modern technological advancements, modern gadgets and
weaponry and such other facilities.
10.7 The Ministry in its written reply has stated that the improvement in police performance due
to modernization, to a considerable extent, will depend on the provision of basic necessary
infrastructure in all the police stations as well as in the district police headquarters. Emphasis is
also being laid on providing IT facilities. A Project called “Common Integrated Police Application”
(CIPA) is being implemented in all the States to ensure a uniform framework and mechanism
for computerization of crime registration, investigation, etc. at the police station level. NIC is
the implementing agency for the project, which is being implemented in all the States in a phased
manner.
10.8 The Ministry giving details about the scheme stated that:—
“CIP A was launched on a pilot basis in 6 police stations in Delhi in the year 2005
and subsequently it was decided to implement the project in the entire country in a
phased manner. Till 2007, out of total of 14000 police stations in the country nearly
1300 police stations were covered under CIP A. The Project is being implemented by
NIC and from 2004-05 till December, 2007, a total amount of Rs.129 crore has been
released to NIC for the implementation of CIPA under the Modernisation of State
Police Forces Scheme”
10.9 It has been further stated by the Ministry that it is proposed to widen the scope of the
CIPA project in terms of the application and by extending it from the police stations to the other
higher level formations in the police hierarchy e.g. the circle/districts/range/zonal offices and the
police headquarters, for consolidating the police station databases at a central location and providing
appropriate software interfaces for interaction and sharing of crime related information. At present,

24
CIPA essentially has crime registration, investigation and prosecution modules. It is now proposed
to provide all functionalities and integrate appropriate technologies, such as, fingerprinting and other
forensic science applications in a large network, so that the information and technology can be
shared by all concerned. For this purpose, the police stations and other higher police formations
are also proposed to be linked through a broadband/CDMA/VSAT network. It has further been
stated by the Ministry that an amount of Rs.2000 crore has been allocated for Eleventh Plan period
by the Planning Commission.
10.10 The new schemes are aimed at efficient and transparent police functioning with better
public service delivery. Some of the areas where technological upgradation of police operations
would directly benefit common people are:
(i) General information to public about police station, District area, jurisdiction, names
and phone numbers of officers, Administrative set-up, Crime and Traffic Advisories,
Public notices, etc.;
(ii) Registration of online complaints;
(iii) Providing information relating to status of case registered at police station;
(iv) Providing information relating to an application, petition or request;
(v) Provide copies of permissible documents like FIR, Post Mortem Report, etc.;
(vi) Coordination of stolen, recovered and seized property;
(vii) Coordination of missing, arrested, unidentified persons, and dead bodies; and
(viii) V erification of persons for employment, domestic help, passport, etc.
10.11 The Scheme is scheduled to be completed in a period of four years commencing from
2008-09. The total financial implications for the implementation of the Plan Scheme are estimated
at Rs.2036.67 crore. The Planning Commission has approved an outlay of Rs.210.00 crore for
the year 2008-09.
10.12 The CIPA scheme is a path breaking initiative in networking the entire policing
system of the country. Now that the scheme is being extended to the entire country and also
to other higher levels of hierarchy of the police system, completion thereof, may bring a
perceptible change in the police public interface and the public perception of it. The
Committee, however, recommends that emphasis should be laid on the attitude and
behaviour of the police personnel. The Committee also desires that the Scheme be
implemented in its true spirit and the targets should be achieved. The Committee also
recommends that a monitoring mechanism should be put in place at the Centre to ensure
proper implementation of the scheme.

Bureau of Immigration (BoI)
13.0 The major role of Bureau of Immigration is to control 11 Immigration Check Posts (ICP)
out of the total 77 ICPs to regulate entry into and exit from the country. The remaining 66 ICPs
are controlled by the State Governments/UT Administration on agency basis on behalf of the
Government of India. Modernisation of 33 ICPs which cater to around 99% of passenger traffic
was initiated in the year 2004-05 for improving the immigration services in the country. The
modernization programme, inter alia, includes upgradation of computer systems; installation of
Immigration Control System (ICS) software; installation of Passport Reading Machines (PRMs);
installation of Questionable Document Examiner (QDE) Machines; and networking of ICPs with
Central Foreigners Bureau (CFB).
13.1 The Ministry stated that with these modern facilities put into place under the modernization
programme, there has been a qualitative improvement in the immigration services in terms of
enhanced security screening of the passengers coupled with expeditious immigration clearance.
13.2 The Ministry further stated that Bureau of Immigration had submitted a proposal for taking
over of 38 ICPs (including the 11 controlled by it) in phases during the FY 2008-09. An enhanced
amount of Rs.57.90 crores was provided to BoI in the BE 2008-09 as compared to an amount of
Rs.28.65 crores in the BE 2007-08 to Complete the modernization programme of 33 ICPs and to
extend the modernization facilities to 5 more ICPs i.e. from 33 to 38.
13.3 The Committee notes the progress made in the modernization of BOIs but feels that
latest equipments are required for upgradation of system like equipments which could be
laser compatible so that it could identify counterfeit currencies, foreign countries passports,
etc. The Committee feels that these days the equipments are becoming more advanced and
the credentials of the individuals could be checked with thumb impression, colour of eye,
blood report, etc. The modernization should be aimed at keeping in view the requirement
for next ten years. The Committee also recommends that all ICPs should be covered under
modernization in a phased manner.

to be shifted to zero line as the people residing along the border line are facing problems in
attending to their agricultural work. The gates of fencing open for very little time and it is difficult

14.1 The Ministry in its response has stated that an amount of Rs.25.47 crore has been estimated

should be initiated at the earliest for shifting of the fence to zero line. The Committee also

Illegal Bangladeshi Migrants
15.0 The porosity of the Indo-Bangladesh border and the practical difficulties due to
topographical reasons acting as impediments in the timely completion of border works’ projects,
are amongst the contributory factors towards influx of illegal Bangladeshi migrants. It has also
been reported that these illegal migrants have been able to secure ration cards, driving licences,
voter identity cards and even PAN cards. Media reports have attributed claims to the intelligence
sources that terrorist groups have been recruiting Bangladeshis in India. It has also been reported
that certain Bangladeshi insurgent groups have been involved in the terrorist incidents in our
country.
15.1 The Ministry in its written response stated that the Government was aware of reports, from
time to time, about illegal immigration into India from Bangladesh. Various measures have been
taken by the Government to check and contain such illegal immigration, which inter alia , includes
the construction of border fencing/flood lighting and roads to enable more effective patrolling, etc.,
assignment of the border guarding duties on the Indo-Bangladesh border to a single force, viz., the
BSF, augmentation of the strength of BSF through additional battalions, reduction of gaps between
border outposts, provision of modern surveillance and other equipment and gadgetry to the BSF,
etc.
15.2 While the above measures are aimed at reducing the possibilities of illegal migration into the
country from across the border, instructions have also been issued to the State Governments and
the UT administration, from time to time, to take sustained action to detect foreign nationals,
including Bangladeshi nationals, staying illegally in the country. 32 Foreigners Tribunals under the
provisions of the Foreigners (Tribunals) Order, 1964 have also been constituted in the State of
Assam for detention of illegal migrants/foreigners.
15.3 The Ministry has also stated that involvement of terrorist groups based in Bangladesh in
some incidents of terrorist violence had come to notice, but there were no reports of recruitment
of Bangladeshi nationals in India for these purposes. Apart from the various measures being taken
within the country for preventing terrorist incidents which, inter alia , include continuous sharing
of information and intelligence with the State Governments, strengthening and upgradation of the
State Police Forces under Police Modernisation Scheme, etc., the issue of involvement of
Bangladesh based terrorist groups in such activities has also been regularly taken up with the
Government of Bangladesh in various bilateral discussions, during which they have been assuring
that the territory of Bangladesh will not be allowed to be used for activities inimical to India.
15.4 The Committee feels that a large presence of illegal Bangladeshi immigrants poses
a grave threat to the internal security and it should be viewed seriously. Reports have also
appeared that counterfeit notes are in large circulation along Indo-Bangladesh border. The
Committee strongly recommends that movement along the border may be strictly
monitored.

Insurgency in North-Eastern States
17.0 The Committee’s attention was drawn to the insurgency in the North-Eastern States. It was
given to understand that most of the insurgent movements in the region pertain to secessionism.
It is not just a law and order problem. Hence it needs to be dealt with separately. Though the
Government have had negotiations with the insurgent groups, but during the negotiations,
insurgents utilized the opportunity for consolidation and their activities were intensified.
17.1 Commenting on this issue, the Home Secretary has submitted as below:
“We entirely agree that this phenomenon is not a law and order phenomenon. It is
something which is very directly connected with the internal security and national security.
Having said that, while, of course, lot of arrangements has been made, there is no question
of leaving it to the State Governments. A lot of additional paramilitary forces have been
provided there. The Border Security Forces have been deployed there. The Army has been
deployed. In Assam, the Armed Forces Special Power Act is in operation which only shows
that it is being treated very differently from a normal law and order situation. .....there is
a very complex situation in terms of different ethnic groups and the competing demands.....
Even in Manipur, there are the Nagas, Kukis and others. So, all these create difficulties.
At one level, we have, certainly, entered into what we call ‘Suspension of Operations
Agreement’ with various outfits in Assam and in certain other States. We have also felt that
some of these groups might try to utilise this period to otherwise strengthen their cadres.
So, one thing which we are very, very seriously and earnestly insisting upon is that wherever
any arrangement of SOO nature is there, these cadres must go to the camps. ......, recently,
there was a problem with one of these groups because the insistence of the security forces
was that they should go into their camps, and they didn’t want to. We are mindful of this.
We are trying to do it. But there are problems; there are limitations. But, if we look at the
overall situation in the North-East, the general level of violence has come down. In the
year 2007, unfortunately, however, there has been an increase in the number of casualties
in Manipur and Assam, particularly. In Assam also, in the earlier part of the year, there
were some targeted attacks in which multiple casualties took place. But we have made it
clear to the State Governments that there is no question of any let-up in terms of
operations. I have, personally, visited Assam and Manipur. The Cabinet Secretary also
would be visiting Assam and Manipur. We are focussing on these States. And, ....., in
Manipur, at least, a part of the area, which is the New Samtal Area, which had remained
under the control of the insurgents, has also been cleared, and we are now trying to put
into that area a civil administration set up. The Assam Rifles posts and positions have been

32
put up there. So, while we, entirely, agree that there is no question of treating this situation
in the North-East as a law and order problem, the Central Government is absolutely and
fully committed to treating this as an internal and national security problem, and we are
trying to deal with it.”
17.2 The Committee feels that for the last four or five decades, this region is facing the
problem of insurgency and people are frustrated with the prevailing situation. The
Government has to take on the responsibility of resolving the problem. The Committee is
of the considered view that inspite of decrease in number of the casualities; reported
instances of extortion activities and collection of levies by the outlawed groups are
increasing. The Committee calls upon the Ministry to keep a close watch on the
developments in this regard and all efforts be made to foil the nefarious design of the
secessionists.

AT A GLANCE
MULTIPURPOSE NATIONAL IDENTITY CARDS SCHEME
The Committee expresses its strong displeasure on the adhocism adopted by the
Government. The MNIC scheme was launched on pilot basis prior to the announcement of
the DID scheme. The Planning Commission should have obtained status as well as feedback
on the MNIC Scheme and then taken a decision on any other scheme, let alone UID
scheme. Running of two parallel schemes appear to be overlapping in objectives and may
be perceived to be wastage of time and resource. Implementation of the pilot project for
MNIC has taken unduly long time and yet it is not known how long it would take to
complete the Scheme in the entire country and on top of that another scheme has been
launched. The Committee recommends that the Group of Ministers may critically review the
MNIC and UID Schemes and examine the feasibility of merging the two into a single
integrated programme, so as to avoid overlapping of objectives and likely wastage of
resource and manpower. Whatever may be the recommendation of the Committee;
Government must ensure that such a programme should be made feasible for
implementation within a reasonable and strictive time frame. (Para 9.4)

appeared that counterfeit notes are in large circulation along Indo-Bangladesh border. The
Committee strongly recommends that movement along the border may be strictly
monitored. (Para 15.4)
BORDER AREA DEVELOPMENT PROGRAMME (BADP)
The Committee in its One Hundred thirteenth Report on Demands for Grants
(2005-06) pertaining to the Ministry of DoNER had recommended that it should specify the
developmental work under the Border Area Development Scheme which should be
undertaken around 60-75 Km of the actual border. But the ground realities in this context
are different as the Committee came to know about the fact that these funds are spent on
civilian gardens and parks depriving the people in the border areas where there is hardly
any communication. The Committee recommends that a proper monitoring mechanism
should be put in place to monitor the utilization of these funds as the people living in the
border areas are suffering due to lack of infrastructure viz. schools and other medical
facilities. (Para 16.2)
The Committee feels that border areas in the North-Eastern part of the country have
been neglected for a long time. Even today some border areas are not easily accessible. The
Committee is constraint to note that in spite of its recommendation made in earlier reports,
the Cabinet Secretariat has not taken any decision on the issue of transferring of BADP
scheme to Ministry of DoNER. The Committee, therefore, recommends that the issue be
resolved immediately in the interest of the nation. (Para 16.8)
INSURGENCY IN NORTH-EASTERN STATES
The Committee feels that for the last four or five decades, this region is facing the
problem of insurgency and people are frustrated with the prevailing situation. The
Government has to take on the responsibility of resolving the problem. The Committee is
of the considered view that inspite of decrease in number of the causalities; reported
instances of extortion activities and collection of levies by the outlawed groups are
increasing. The Committee calls upon the Ministry to keep a close watch on the
developments in this regard and all efforts be made to foil the nefarious design of the
secessionists. (Para 17.2)
